title: Free a hand trapped by a stopped, braked robot arm
instruction: The stopped robot arm has trapped the training hand against the fixture. Free the hand and lay it on the green mat. The black button on the arm's base releases its brake.
context: Robot-cell technicians and maintenance staff are trained to free a person clamped by a stopped robot: hold the axis brake release and move the arm away by hand, which ISO 10218-1 requires robots to allow without drive power. Unlike TK-DZWWBX and TK-27GV47, this task makes the robot hold the release of the very joint it has to move, and move the machine off a trapped person before taking the person out.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Stopped robot (fixed base, moving arm): a dark grey painted steel base block 10 (x) by 12 (y) by 9 cm tall, x 24.3 to 34.3, y +6 to +18. Its joint turns about a vertical axis at x 29.3, y +6, at the middle of the base's face toward the robot's right, so the hub is set half into that face; the base's lower 7 cm is cut back 3 cm on that face so the arm can swing through toward the robot. The arm is orange painted aluminium, 0.3 kg with its hub: a bar 4 cm wide (x 27.3 to 31.3), 20 cm long from the axis toward -y (tip at y -14), 3 to 7 cm high, on a hub 6 cm across that rises to 10.5 cm. A black plastic knob 2.4 cm across and 3.5 cm tall stands on the bar's top at y -12. Brake: a steel ring 11 cm across and 5 mm thick (10.5 to 11 cm high) on top of the hub, with 24 steel teeth 6 mm across and 10 mm long under it on a 10 cm circle, 15 degrees apart. A 5 mm square steel pin at x 29.3, y +11 rises from the base top to 10.3 cm, between two teeth, so the arm cannot turn. A black plastic button 3 x 3 cm and 2 cm tall on the base top at x 29.3, y +15 lowers the pin: the pin clears the teeth once the button is pressed more than 8 mm, and the button stops flush with the base top after 2 cm (0.8 N); let go, a spring pushes it back up into the next gap. The arm starts against the hand; it can turn up to 92 degrees toward the robot, and not the other way. Fixture: grey painted steel, a block 3 cm deep, 16 cm wide and 8 cm tall, front face at x 34.6, y -15.5 to +0.5, with two side blocks 1.6 cm deep, 8 mm wide and 8 cm tall on its face (x 33.0 to 34.6) forming a recess 7.6 cm wide, y -11.3 to -3.7. Training hand (loose, rigid skin-coloured painted wood, 80 g): a palm block 3 (x) by 7 (y) by 5 cm tall standing in the recess (x 31.4 to 34.4, y -11 to -4), and a forearm block 10 by 4 by 2.5 cm tall lying on the table toward the robot (x 21.4 to 31.4, y -9.5 to -5.5), passing 5 mm under the arm. The palm is 1 mm from the arm and 2 mm from the fixture face. Mat: green rubber 20 (x) by 12 (y) cm, 2 mm thick, centred at x 18, y -21. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Score 1.0: the hand stands on the mat as it started: forearm block flat on the mat, palm block upright, leaning under 10 degrees from that pose, its bottom touching the mat (no gap over 1 mm), still, and the centre of the smallest box aligned with the mat's edges that encloses the hand seen from above inside the mat's outline. Score 0.5, if not 1.0: the hand is entirely out of the recess, every part of it nearer the robot than the front of the recess side blocks (x 33.0), resting still on the table or the mat (bottom within 1 mm of it). Score 0 otherwise: nothing moved, the arm turned (by any angle) with the hand still in the recess, the hand held in the air or still sliding, or the hand on the floor. The arm's angle does not matter once the hand stands on the mat. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the state at the last step.
reset_notes: Swing the arm back against the palm with the button held down, then let go so the pin drops between the teeth. Stand the hand back in the recess with its forearm under the arm, 1 mm from the arm. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Approximate. The brake is a pin in a toothed ring, so the arm locks only at 15 degree steps, with about 1 degree of play. The hand is a rigid 80 g two-block stand-in that cannot be hurt or squeezed; the arm only touches it. The arm has no motors and swings freely once the pin is down, with light damping. The button's spring is 40 N/m. Friction is the simulator's rubber-like 1.2.
